speaker: Unknown
en: Hi, I'm Connie Loizis.
zh: 嗨,我是 Connie Loizis。

speaker: Unknown
en: And this is Alex Gove.
zh: 这是 Alex Gove。

speaker: Unknown
en: And this is Strictly VC Download.
zh: 这是 Strictly VC Download。

speaker: Unknown
en: Hello, and welcome back to Strictly VC Download.
zh: 大家好,欢迎回到 Strictly VC Download。

speaker: Unknown
en: Today's conversation was recorded live at our Strictly VC event in New York on Thursday night, September 10th, where I sat down with Keith Raboy, Managing Director at Coastal Ventures.
zh: 今天的对话录制于 9 月 10 日周四晚上我们在纽约举办的 Strictly VC 活动,现场我与 Coastal Ventures 董事总经理 Keith Raboy 进行了对谈。

speaker: Unknown
en: I don't get to talk with Raboy very often and I always enjoy it.
zh: 我不常和 Raboy 聊天,但我总是很享受。

speaker: Unknown
en: I'm always stunned by how fast he speaks and how quickly he covers as much ground as he does.
zh: 他说话之快、覆盖话题之广,总是让我惊叹。

speaker: Unknown
en: In this conversation, we get into his bullish outlook on AI.
zh: 在这次对话中,我们谈到了他对 AI 的看好态度。

speaker: Unknown
en: More specifically, as you'll hear, we discussed what he thinks of former Anthropic researcher Jacob Coxon's recent comments about the dangers of AI, and he doesn't think much of them.
zh: 更具体地说,正如你们将听到的,我们讨论了他对前 Anthropic 研究员 Jacob Coxon 近期关于 AI 危险性言论的看法,而他并不怎么买账。

speaker: Unknown
en: We also talked about why he's spending more time in New York, whether he approves of companies that use annualized revenue numbers to land press, even as these numbers are highly unreliable.
zh: 我们还谈到了为什么他花更多时间在纽约,以及他是否认可那些用年化收入数字来博取媒体报道的公司,即便这些数字高度不可靠。

speaker: Unknown
en: And we spent some time on what Raboy looks for when deciding which founders to back.
zh: 我们还花了一些时间谈 Raboy 在决定支持哪些创始人时看重什么。

speaker: Unknown
en: That sounds easy enough, but in a world that's rife with fancy degrees and people who are at ease telling a good story about their vision, I do think it's a lot harder than it looks.
zh: 这听起来够简单的,但在一个充斥着名牌学位、且人们能轻松把自己的愿景讲成动听故事的世界里,我确实认为这比看上去难得多。

speaker: Unknown
en: And it was interesting to hear about one of his hacks on this front.
zh: 而听到他在这一点上的一个诀窍,很有意思。

speaker: Unknown
en: In any case, we hope you enjoyed this conversation with Keith Raboy as much as we did.
zh: 无论如何,希望你们和我们一样享受这次与 Keith Raboy 的对话。

speaker: Unknown
en: If you missed this Strictly VC evening, we hope you can make it to the next one.
zh: 如果你错过了这次 Strictly VC 之夜,希望你下次能来。

speaker: Unknown
en: And either way, we will see you back here next week.
zh: 不管怎样,下周再见。

speaker: Unknown
en: Thank you so much for coming.
zh: 非常感谢你来。

speaker: Unknown
en: Pleasure to be with you.
zh: 很高兴和你在一起。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's been a long time.
zh: 好久不见了。

speaker: Unknown
en: It has been a long time.
zh: 确实好久不见了。

speaker: Unknown
en: We didn't have an agenda, and you're always so great at your game for anything.
zh: 我们没有准备议程,而你在任何话题上总是很在行。

speaker: Unknown
en: I thought we could talk about maybe the news of the week, which has me freaked out, candidly.
zh: 我想我们可以聊聊本周的新闻,坦白说,这让我很慌。

speaker: Unknown
en: Which day of the week?
zh: 一周里的哪一天?

speaker: Unknown
en: I know.
zh: 我知道。

speaker: Unknown
en: I guess, let's see, Monday, what is it?
zh: 我猜,让我看看,周一,是什么来着?

speaker: Unknown
en: Was it Thursday?
zh: 是周四吗?

speaker: Unknown
en: The former Anthropic researcher who was also at OpenAI previously said,
zh: 那位前 Anthropic 研究员,他之前也在 OpenAI 待过,说——

speaker: Unknown
en: On his way out to the door of Anthropic in a, you know, a tweet storm, these companies are gambling with our lives, after which I'm sure you saw another Anthropic researcher weighed in and said, yeah, he's not kidding, and we think there's like a 10% chance that it's going to kill all of us in what, like, I don't know, soon.
zh: 在他离开 Anthropic 的门口,在一场你知道的推文风暴里——"这些公司在拿我们的生命赌博",之后我确信你看到了另一位 Anthropic 研究员跟进说,是的,他不是在开玩笑,我们认为有大概 10% 的概率它会杀死我们所有人,在什么时候来着,我不知道,很快。

speaker: Unknown
en: I've been really unsettled by that.
zh: 这让我一直很不安。

speaker: Unknown
en: What are you thinking?
zh: 你是怎么想的?

speaker: Unknown
en: What are your friends thinking or talking about in reaction?
zh: 你的朋友们对此的反应或谈论是什么?

speaker: Unknown
en: I mean, personally, I'm a tech optimist and I don't think you should be in this profession unless you believe that tech is this magic wand that improves society.
zh: 我的意思是,就我个人而言,我是个技术乐观主义者,我认为如果你不相信技术是改善社会的魔杖,你就不该干这一行。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so that's what we do.
zh: 这就是我们所做的事。

speaker: Unknown
en: I give people capital and sometimes useful advice and ask them to take the magic wand of tech and fix things.
zh: 我给人们资金,有时提供有用的建议,请他们拿起技术这根魔杖去解决问题。

speaker: Unknown
en: And anybody who doesn't believe that tech is generally good and that tech can improve all of our lives, our kids' lives, my kids' lives, shouldn't be in tech.
zh: 任何不相信技术总体上是好的、不相信技术能改善我们所有人生活、我们孩子的生活、我孩子生活的人,都不该待在科技行业。

speaker: Unknown
en: They shouldn't be investing and they shouldn't be an entrepreneur and they shouldn't be working at a company that's building things through tech.
zh: 他们不该做投资,不该当创业者,也不该在一家通过技术造东西的公司工作。

speaker: Unknown
en: Fortunately, there's enough talented people that believe in the optimistic view of the world that almost all human progress for the last four centuries has been driven by technology.
zh: 幸运的是,有足够多有才华的人相信这种对世界的乐观看法,即过去四个世纪几乎所有的人类进步都是由技术驱动的。

speaker: Unknown
en: Now, it's more recent, the last 50 years, it's been driven through what we think of as startups or in venture capital-fueled startups, but all human progress.
zh: 现在,更近一些,最近 50 年,是由我们所说的初创公司或风投资助的初创公司驱动的,但所有的人类进步——

speaker: Unknown
en: lives have been improved through tech, whether it was the industrial revolution or the railroad, everything we take for granted, and that we're not toiling on, you know, the fields from like 4 a.m. to whatever time, and that we have choices in our life about moving around the globe or moving around the country and, you know, marrying people we like versus people we're
zh: 生活都是通过技术得到改善的,无论是工业革命还是铁路,我们所习以为常的一切,我们不用在你知道的凌晨 4 点到什么时候在田里劳作,我们在生活中可以选择环游全球或环游全国,可以选择和你喜欢的人结婚,而不是——

speaker: Unknown
en: Forced to by our parents is all a function of tech revolutions.
zh: 被父母强迫的人,这些都是技术革命的产物。

speaker: Unknown
en: And this is gonna continue, you know, and then also the zero defect philosophy just doesn't make any sense to me.
zh: 而且这会继续下去,你知道的,另外零缺陷哲学在我看来完全说不通。

speaker: Unknown
en: If you go out the street right now, there's a non-zero chance that some Uber driver runs you over.
zh: 如果你现在走到街上,有非零的概率某个 Uber 司机会撞到你。

speaker: Unknown
en: Several people in this room sometime in the next 20 years unfortunately will have something like a heart attack.
zh: 未来 20 年内,这个房间里的几个人不幸会经历类似心脏病发作的事情。

speaker: Unknown
en: You can slip in your shower.
zh: 你可能在淋浴时滑倒。

speaker: Unknown
en: Like living your life thinking about everything that can go wrong is just a nonsensical way to live in my view.
zh: 在我看来,过日子时想着所有可能出错的事,是一种荒谬的活法。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so I also don't
zh: 所以我也不

speaker: Unknown
en: believe that some chance that something goes wrong is a reason to hit brakes on everything.
zh: 相信某种事情出错的可能性是给一切踩刹车的理由。

speaker: Unknown
en: I think you can be thoughtful, careful, intelligent, but we need to improve the world.
zh: 我认为你可以深思熟虑、谨慎、聪明,但我们需要改善世界。

speaker: Unknown
en: And if we don't improve the world through technology, other people that we don't like, and we don't like their values, and we don't believe that they celebrate or recognize human dignity, are going to take advantage of technology, and we're going to wind up in a world we don't like.
zh: 如果我们不通过技术改善世界,那些我们不喜欢的人、我们不认同其价值观的人、我们不认为他们尊重或承认人的尊严的人,会利用技术,而我们最终会生活在一个我们不喜欢的世界里。

speaker: Unknown
en: This is the lesson of every history.
zh: 这是每一部历史的教训。

speaker: Unknown
en: And, you know, some people superficially allude to, you know, kind of World War II and they watched some dumb movie called Oppenheimer.
zh: 而且，你知道，有些人很表面地提及，你知道，某种二战，他们看了一部叫《奥本海默》的蠢电影。

speaker: Unknown
en: And you're like, oh my God.
zh: 然后你会想，哦我的天。

speaker: Unknown
en: The lesson from Oppenheimer is, first of all, what would the world look like if Germans had invented a nuclear bomb before we did?
zh: 《奥本海默》的教训是，首先，如果德国人在我们之前发明了核弹，世界会是什么样子？

speaker: Unknown
en: That would not be very pretty.
zh: 那不会太好。

speaker: Unknown
en: And it could have happened.
zh: 而且这本来可能发生。

speaker: Unknown
en: Fortunately, most of the German scientists who were any good were Jewish.
zh: 幸运的是，大多数有点本事的德国科学家都是犹太人。

speaker: Unknown
en: And they were either forced or consciously chose to leave the country, or we would have confronted a very serious problem, or what would the world have looked like if the Soviet Union had nuclear capabilities way before the United States?
zh: 他们要么被迫，要么有意识地选择离开那个国家，否则我们就会面临一个非常严重的问题，或者如果苏联远远早于美国就拥有了核能力，世界会是什么样子？

speaker: Unknown
en: The other thing about nuclear capabilities is arguably the last 50, 60, 70 years, 80 years of the modern era have been more peaceful than at any period in human history.
zh: 关于核能力的另一件事是，可以说现代最近 50、60、70、80 年比人类历史上任何时期都更加和平。

speaker: Unknown
en: As a percentage of population, people dying through conflict has gone down after the advent of the nuclear bomb.
zh: 按人口百分比计算，核弹出现之后，死于冲突的人已经下降了。

speaker: Unknown
en: So things that people think are potentially catastrophic, they're potentially threatening, could exterminate all people, et cetera, have turned out to basically stabilize the world and make it more likely that you're going to live a normal lifespan.
zh: 所以那些人们认为可能带来灾难、可能构成威胁、可能消灭所有人的东西，等等，结果基本上稳定了世界，并使你更有可能活到正常的寿命。

speaker: Unknown
en: So again, I wouldn't overthink this.
zh: 所以再说一次，我不会想太多。

speaker: Unknown
en: The last thing is the worst people in the world to sort of navigate this is often asking the government to intervene.
zh: 最后一点，世界上最不适合来处理这件事的人，往往是要求政府介入的人。

speaker: Unknown
en: Like I don't trust the DMV.
zh: 比如我不信任车管所。

speaker: Unknown
en: I don't trust the government with my health care.
zh: 我不信任政府来管我的医疗。

speaker: Unknown
en: I wouldn't trust the government with anything.
zh: 我不会把任何东西交给政府。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so I know most of the people who serve in the federal government actually, the executive branch certainly, and I like many of them.
zh: 而且我其实认识大多数在联邦政府、当然在行政部门任职的人，我喜欢他们中的很多人。

speaker: Unknown
en: But would I rather take 10 people from Silicon Valley or 10 people from the executive branch?
zh: 但我是更愿意从硅谷拿 10 个人，还是从行政部门拿 10 个人？

speaker: Unknown
en: It's not so obvious who I'd want to make decisions about the future of mankind.
zh: 至于我想让谁来决定人类的未来，这并不那么明显。

speaker: Unknown
en: Yeah, and I'm sure a lot of people here would agree with you, but I do think that we're talking about something that's unprecedented.
zh: 是的，我相信这里很多人都会同意你，但我确实认为我们在谈论的是某种前所未有的东西。

speaker: Unknown
en: Also, the details matter here.
zh: 另外，细节在这里很重要。

speaker: Unknown
en: This is basically an intern.
zh: 这基本上就是一个实习生。

speaker: Unknown
en: He worked there six weeks, most surely funded by China.
zh: 他在那里工作了六周，十有八九是由中国资助的。

speaker: Unknown
en: I think that's all starting to play out.
zh: 我觉得这一切都开始上演了。

speaker: Unknown
en: Is there six weeks?
zh: 是六周吗？

speaker: Unknown
en: Yeah, he literally worked at Anthropic for six weeks.
zh: 是的，他真的在 Anthropic 只工作了六周。

speaker: Unknown
en: How long did he work at OpenAI?
zh: 他在 OpenAI 工作了多久？

speaker: Unknown
en: I don't know.
zh: 我不知道。

speaker: Unknown
en: That's interesting.
zh: 这很有意思。

speaker: Unknown
en: I did not know that.
zh: 我之前不知道这个。

speaker: Unknown
en: But what I was going to say is I wonder about how to talk to my kids about this.
zh: 但我本来要说的是，我在想该如何跟我的孩子们谈论这件事。

speaker: Unknown
en: And what's difficult for me is the fact that the founders of these companies, Sam and Dario, say also there is this risk.
zh: 而对我来说困难的是，这些公司的创始人，Sam 和 Dario，也说过确实存在这种风险。

speaker: Unknown
en: Well, I think they just need to communicate better.
zh: 嗯，我觉得他们只是需要更好地沟通。

speaker: Unknown
en: First of all, Sam particularly has got much better at this and AI is going to transform so many positive things.
zh: 首先，Sam 尤其在这方面做得好多了，而且 AI 将改变非常多积极的事情。

speaker: Unknown
en: You're seeing this play out in medicine and bio, but the net effect also is very important.
zh: 你可以看到这在医学和生物领域正在上演，但净效应也非常重要。

speaker: Unknown
en: Like the way I think about it, I have a five-year-old, actually boy and girl, but the boy is into rockets.
zh: 比如我是这么想的，我有一个五岁的孩子，其实是龙凤胎，男孩喜欢火箭。

speaker: Unknown
en: I believe that by the time he's finishing high school, 13 years from today,
zh: 我相信等他高中毕业时，也就是距今 13 年后，

speaker: Unknown
en: His high school project will actually be put a rocket onto some planet, like the moon.
zh: 他的高中项目将真的是把一枚火箭送上某个星球，比如月球。

speaker: Unknown
en: The rate of progress and the ability of access to information, that's going to be his high school project.
zh: 进步的速度和信息获取的能力，那将会是他的高中项目。

speaker: Unknown
en: And think about what the world's like when high school kids are putting rockets to the moon.
zh: 想想当高中生都能把火箭送上月球时，世界会是什么样子。

speaker: Unknown
en: So, okay, in terms of regulation, there's different flavors, you know, Anthropic thinks it needs to be regulated by states, which are a little bit heavier-handed.
zh: 所以，好吧，在监管方面，有不同的风格，你知道，Anthropic 认为它需要由各州来监管，这会稍微更严厉一些。

speaker: Unknown
en: I think Sam has said basically he wants for the federal government to take a look at what they're using or developing in return for, like, not regulating it more heavily.
zh: 我想 Sam 基本上说过，他希望联邦政府去看看他们正在使用或开发的东西，作为交换，比如，不对它进行更严厉的监管。

speaker: Unknown
en: But you think zero regulation?
zh: 但你认为应该零监管？

speaker: Unknown
en: I mean, you must...
zh: 我是说，你肯定……

speaker: Unknown
en: For the most part, I think there is a transitional moment right now that is being dealt with reasonably well by the federal government and some of the leading research labs, which is the ability to crack things that we thought were secure.
zh: 在很大程度上，我认为现在有一个过渡时刻，目前由联邦政府和一些领先的研究实验室处理得还算不错，那就是破解那些我们曾认为安全的东西的能力。

speaker: Unknown
en: You can talk about different versions of this, but fundamentally, everybody five years ago was worried about quantum computing, basically undermining all the cryptography, and that still may happen too.
zh: 你可以谈这个的不同版本，但从根本上说，五年前每个人都在担心量子计算，基本上会破坏所有密码学，而这仍然可能发生。

speaker: Unknown
en: But it was going to take a long enough time that most systems now, they're kind of pseudo-quantum computing.
zh: 但那需要足够长的时间，以至于现在的大多数系统，它们有点像伪量子计算。

speaker: Unknown
en: The same thing is going to happen to some extent in the short term with AI.
zh: 同样的事情在短期内也会在一定程度上发生在 AI 身上。

speaker: Unknown
en: The offensive capabilities and the ability to crack things will make systems vulnerable.
zh: 进攻能力和破解东西的能力会使系统变得脆弱。

speaker: Unknown
en: That said, the defensive uses of AI actually may turn out to be superior.
zh: 话虽如此，AI 的防御性用途实际上可能会被证明更胜一筹。

speaker: Unknown
en: The reason why things can be hacked is usually a human flaw.
zh: 东西能被黑的原因通常是人类自身的缺陷。

speaker: Unknown
en: Someone who is building a system didn't think about certain interactions or corner cases or made a just pure mistake.
zh: 构建系统的人没有考虑到某些交互或边界情况，或者纯粹犯了错误。

speaker: Unknown
en: AI-based code and development should eliminate those and reduce the surface area for vulnerabilities, or at least you can make a pretty strong argument.
zh: 基于 AI 的代码和开发应该能消除这些问题，减少漏洞的攻击面，或者至少你可以提出一个相当有力的论证。

speaker: Unknown
en: So as the offensive and defensive capabilities sort of normalize, it's not clear that things are going to be much more vulnerable to attacks in the way people are thinking about vulnerabilities right now.
zh: 所以随着攻防能力某种程度上的正常化，目前还不清楚事情是否会像人们现在想象漏洞的方式那样更容易受到攻击。

speaker: Unknown
en: This always happens in military.
zh: 这种情况在军事领域一直在发生。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's playing out with drones right now.
zh: 现在无人机领域正在上演这一点。

speaker: Unknown
en: Right now, the offensive capabilities of drones are exceedingly the defensive capabilities for the most part, certainly if you adjust and normalize for cost.
zh: 目前，无人机的进攻能力在很大程度上远超防御能力，当然，如果你按成本进行调整和归一化的话。

speaker: Unknown
en: Where that stabilizes, nobody knows.
zh: 局势会在哪里稳定下来，没人知道。

speaker: Unknown
en: And this is the battle through any potential technology that has military applications forever.
zh: 这是任何有军事应用的潜在技术永恒的博弈。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so I wouldn't assume that just because today it opens up some exploits, that it's going to drive more offensive interactions than defensive over time.
zh: 所以我不会仅仅因为今天它打开了一些漏洞利用，就认为随着时间推移它会推动更多进攻性而非防御性的互动。

speaker: Unknown
en: I also just wanted to ask— That's why I'm an optimist.
zh: 我还想问一下—— 这就是为什么我是个乐观主义者。

speaker: Unknown
en: I wanted to ask, speaking of that, you're a friend of Sam Altman.
zh: 我想问的是，说到这个，你是 Sam Altman 的朋友。

speaker: Unknown
en: Your firm is the first institutional investor in OpenAI.
zh: 你的公司是 OpenAI 的第一家机构投资人。

speaker: Unknown
en: I saw the trailer for Artificial this week, and it looks bad.
zh: 我这周看了《Artificial》的预告片，看起来很糟糕。

speaker: Unknown
en: I mean, it's obviously going to portray him as a kook.
zh: 我是说，它显然会把他描绘成一个怪人。

speaker: Unknown
en: I just wonder if you worry about him, because I feel like the narrative in the public sphere is Dario, good guy, Sam Altman, like, you know, Satan.
zh: 我只是想知道你是否为他担心，因为我觉得公共舆论场的叙事是:Dario 是好人，Sam Altman 就像，你知道的，撒旦。

speaker: Unknown
en: Really?
zh: 真的吗?

speaker: Unknown
en: I mean, at least the people I hang out with think Dario's bad and Sam's good, but certainly the people I hang out with in DC believe that.
zh: 我是说，至少我交往的人里认为 Dario 是坏的、Sam 是好的，当然我在华盛顿特区交往的人是这么认为的。

speaker: Unknown
en: Anthropic's very unpopular with most elected officials, actually on both sides of the aisle, for different reasons in some ways, but their ideology is very offensive, and just the way Dario communicates.
zh: Anthropic 实际上在大多数民选官员中非常不受欢迎，其实在两党中都是如此，某种程度上原因各不相同，但他们的意识形态非常冒犯性，还有 Dario 的沟通方式。

speaker: Unknown
en: Both of them talking about job loss,

speaker: Unknown

zh: 当然这不意味着 10 年、20 年、30 年后情况不会改变，但那样的话，如果你在预测这些变化，责任就在于指出拐点是什么、驱动因素是什么、是什么输入导致等式发生改变。

speaker: Unknown
en: As far as I can tell, none of these people are doing
zh: 据我所知，这些人没有一个在

speaker: Unknown
en: The economy in the United States right now is being powered by AI.

zh: 幸运的是，因为经济的其他部分必然有些更不稳，AI 正在产生生产率提升，这带来了就业，为那些在以往许多次技术革命中被排除在外的人带来了高薪工作。

speaker: Unknown
en: Like the best opportunities right now are more in the trades.
zh: 比如现在最好的机会更多在技能型行业里。

speaker: Unknown
en: And these are high-paying 2x, 3x the median income of the United States.
zh: 而且这些是高薪的，是美国收入中位数的 2 倍、3 倍。

speaker: Unknown
en: So this is really exciting.
zh: 所以这真的很令人兴奋。

speaker: Unknown
en: People need to talk about that, plus the medical benefits.
zh: 人们需要谈论这些，再加上医疗方面的好处。

speaker: Unknown
en: Like the kinds of things that kill us and that killed my parents' generation, grandparents' generation, probably are not going to affect us.
zh: 比如那些曾杀死我们、杀死我父母那一代人、祖父母那一代人的疾病，可能不会影响到我们。

speaker: Unknown
en: Now, yes, humans may still have, you know, some lifespan.
zh: 当然，是的，人类可能仍然有，你知道的，一定的寿命。

speaker: Unknown
en: You may not live for, you know, eternity or something.
zh: 你可能不会，你知道的，永生之类的。

speaker: Unknown
en: But I think we're all going to live healthier, happier lives because of AI.
zh: 但我认为我们都会因为 AI 而活得更健康、更快乐。

speaker: Unknown
en: Oh yeah, absolutely.
zh: 哦对，绝对是的。

speaker: Unknown
en: The biotech startups that we are starting to see are mind-blowing.
zh: 我们开始看到的那些生物科技初创公司简直令人惊叹。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I also think the explosion of entrepreneurship driven by AI is going to be really exciting if we survive.
zh: 而且我还认为，由 AI 驱动的创业浪潮会非常令人兴奋，如果我们能幸存下来的话。

speaker: Unknown
en: But on a lighter note, we are sitting here in New York.
zh: 不过说点轻松的，我们现在坐在纽约。

speaker: Unknown
en: What are you doing in New York?
zh: 你在纽约做什么?

speaker: Unknown
en: So a complicated story.

speaker: Unknown
en: I mean, New York's a great entrepreneurial environment.
zh: 我是说，纽约是个很棒的创业环境。

speaker: Unknown
en: Over the last six years, the number one geo that I've invested in, five of the six years, has actually been New York.
zh: 过去六年里，我投资的第一大地区，六年里有五年，实际上是纽约。

speaker: Unknown
en: This year we'll see, depends whether you wait by dollars or kind of investments, but it's a little bit more open this year.
zh: 今年再看吧，取决于你是按美元算还是按投资笔数算，但今年稍微更开放一些。

speaker: Unknown
en: More personal reason, my family works, you know, in DC, goes to school in DC, and it's very difficult to commute from either SF or Miami every week.

speaker: Unknown
en: To DC, where it's very feasible to go every week or every weekend to DC.

speaker: Unknown

speaker: Unknown
en: It's a good reason.
zh: 这是个好理由。

speaker: Unknown
en: Yeah, but there are great companies here.
zh: 是啊，而且这里有很多很棒的公司。

speaker: Unknown
en: Like, you know, Ramp is here as an example.

speaker: Unknown
en: Rogo, you know, we just announced financing this morning.

speaker: Unknown
en: We have lots of application layer.

speaker: Unknown
en: We have lots of financial services, innovative companies like Imprint that are wonderful companies, all based in New York.
zh: 我们有很多金融服务领域的创新公司，比如 Imprint,它们都是很棒的公司，全都位于纽约。

speaker: Unknown
en: So I think this is a great entrepreneurial place to invest, but I don't really have a choice where I am right now.
zh: 所以我认为这是一个非常适合创业投资的地方，但我现在其实没有选择的余地。

speaker: Unknown
en: Do you think the density of talent is the same here?
zh: 你觉得这里的人才密度和那边一样吗？

speaker: Unknown
en: Depends on what role and at what level of seniority.
zh: 取决于什么职位以及什么资历级别。

speaker: Unknown
en: Individual contributor level right out of school, absolutely.
zh: 刚毕业的个人贡献者级别，绝对一样。

speaker: Unknown
en: Arguably, this is what is powered ramp.
zh: 可以说，这正是 Ramp 的动力所在。

speaker: Unknown
en: We've been tapping into right out of school graduates and been able to create a critical density of talent from the intern class on that is extraordinary.
zh: 我们一直在吸纳刚毕业的毕业生，并且从实习生那一届开始就打造出了一种极其出色的关键人才密度。

speaker: Unknown
en: There's these rankings of intern classes and we always rank number one.
zh: 有一些实习生班级的排名，我们总是排名第一。

speaker: Unknown
en: Senior engineers who are architect level, no.
zh: 而架构师级别的资深工程师，不行。

speaker: Unknown
en: I think that's a challenge.
zh: 我认为这是一个挑战。

speaker: Unknown
en: Fortunately,
zh: 幸运的是，

speaker: Unknown
en: Maybe in the modern age you need less of these people per company than you have historically, but that's a challenge.
zh: 也许在当今时代，每家公司需要这类人的数量比历史上少，但这仍然是个挑战。

speaker: Unknown
en: Senior executives is also a challenge.
zh: 高管层也是一个挑战。

speaker: Unknown
en: If you have an in-office culture, most of these more senior people that live and reside in the New York area live outside the city, and the commute in and out of the city for an office environment can be very painful.
zh: 如果你有办公室文化，这些居住在纽约地区的较资深的人大多住在市外，为办公室环境每天进出城市通勤可能非常痛苦。

speaker: Unknown
en: I grew up in a commuter suburb of New York, so I'm very familiar with this.
zh: 我在纽约的一个通勤郊区长大，所以我对此非常熟悉。

speaker: Unknown
en: We were like 32 minutes express train into the city, but many people live, you know, two concentric circles further away.
zh: 我们坐快线火车进城大约 32 分钟，但很多人住得更远，你知道的，还要再往外两个同心圈。

speaker: Unknown
en: So when you need to recruit proven executive talent and you really believe in an in-office culture, those two things have been very challenging.
zh: 所以当你需要招募经过验证的高管人才，而你又真心信奉办公室文化时，这两件事一直非常有挑战。

speaker: Unknown
en: The way we solve this at RAMP specifically is we don't hire senior people.
zh: 我们在 RAMP 具体的解决方式是，我们不招资深的人。

speaker: Unknown
en: We just build from the bottom up, ground up.
zh: 我们只是从下往上、从零开始培养。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's been a very conscious strategy very intentionally for the last three years.
zh: 过去三年，这一直是一个非常自觉、非常有意的策略。

speaker: Unknown
en: That can work.
zh: 这是行得通的。

speaker: Unknown
en: But if you need a CFO, SVP of sales, someone who's got a lot of gravitas and experience, it's really hard to have them in the office five days a week because unless they're very independently wealthy, they really can't afford to raise a family like right in the middle of the city.
zh: 但如果你需要一个 CFO、销售 SVP,某个有很多分量和经验的人，让他们每周五天来办公室真的很难，因为除非他们非常富有独立，否则真的负担不起就在市中心养家。

speaker: Unknown
en: And are you going to be a lone wolf, or is there more to come?
zh: 那你打算做一匹独狼，还是会有更多动作？

speaker: Unknown
en: We're opening an office.
zh: 我们要开一个办公室。

speaker: Unknown
en: So Katie is opening an office on 14th Street.
zh: Katie 要在第 14 街开一个办公室。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's actually allegedly being built out now.
zh: 据说现在实际上正在装修中。

speaker: Unknown
en: We'll see.
zh: 到时候看吧。

speaker: Unknown
en: This fall opening date is very vague in my mind.
zh: 今年秋天的开业日期在我脑海里非常模糊。

speaker: Unknown
en: I'll have a couple colleagues here with me, and they were also opening up what's called an executive briefing center.
zh: 我会有几位同事和我一起在这里，而且他们还要开设一个所谓的行政简报中心。

speaker: Unknown
en: Which is where we matchmake a set of portfolio companies, say 10 or 12 at a time, with a Fortune 500 company.
zh: 在那里，我们把一批被投公司，比如一次 10 到 12 家，与一家财富 500 强公司进行对接。

speaker: Unknown
en: And we're gonna do that four days a week.
zh: 我们打算每周做四天。

speaker: Unknown
en: And portfolio companies love this.

speaker: Unknown
en: You know, they get pilots and customers.
zh: 你知道的，他们能获得试点和客户。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so it's gonna be a very vibrant office because of that.
zh: 正因如此，这会是一个非常热闹的办公室。

speaker: Unknown
en: There'll only be a handful of investors here, hopefully.
zh: 但希望这里只会有一小撮投资人。

speaker: Unknown
en: This is the first time that KB's really ever left 2128 Sand Hill Road.
zh: 这是 KB 第一次真正离开 2128 Sand Hill Road。

speaker: Unknown
en: We don't even have an SF office.
zh: 我们连 SF 的办公室都没有。

speaker: Unknown
en: So this is a very big step for us.
zh: 所以这对我们来说是非常大的一步。

speaker: Unknown
en: You know, you mentioned Ramp.
zh: 你知道的，你提到了 Ramp。

speaker: Unknown
en: I know that's a big investment of yours through Coastal and Founders Fund where you spent some time.
zh: 我知道那是你通过 Coastal 和 Founders Fund 做的一笔重要投资，你曾在那里待过一段时间。

speaker: Unknown
en: I think Ramp is so brilliant in ways, including getting press.
zh: 我认为 Ramp 在很多方面都非常出色，包括吸引媒体报道。

speaker: Unknown
en: But sometimes I find it a little unsettling.
zh: 但有时我觉得它有点让人不安。

speaker: Unknown
en: I mean, the talk about ARRs, which I know a lot of founders in the audience probably also rely on as a means of attracting attention, annualized revenue, what do you think of that strategy?
zh: 我的意思是，谈到 ARR,我知道现场很多创始人可能也依赖它作为吸引关注的一种手段，即年化营收，你怎么看那种策略？

speaker: Unknown
en: It depends.
zh: 看情况。

speaker: Unknown
en: Founders kind of have different preferences.
zh: 创始人们的偏好各不相同。

speaker: Unknown
en: The value of transparency is you show the momentum, you get press coverage, you get recruiting.
zh: 透明的价值在于你展示了势头，你获得媒体报道，你获得招聘优势。

speaker: Unknown
en: The downside that I cautioned founders in the beginning about that level of transparency ultimately is every company has blitz.
zh: 而我一开始就提醒创始人的那种透明度的坏处，归根结底是每家公司都有 blitz(高速扩张期)。

speaker: Unknown
en: And it's not so fun to have your metrics public when you're suffering through a roller coaster ride.
zh: 当你在过山车式的煎熬中挣扎时，让你的指标公开可没那么好玩。

speaker: Unknown
en: So yeah, the success case, it's great, but you should plan for how are you going to manage.
zh: 所以是的，成功的情况下，这很棒，但你应该提前想好你要如何应对。

speaker: Unknown
en: And public companies obviously deal with this all the time, but many companies, when they're earlier, are not set up, they're not insulated, they're not immune, they're not sophisticated enough, they're not mature enough to deal with that downside risk.
zh: 上市公司显然一直在处理这种情况，但很多公司在早期阶段并没有做好准备，没有隔离层，没有免疫力，不够老练，不够成熟，无法应对那种下行风险。

speaker: Unknown
en: So I think there's sometimes founders are overly optimistic about sharing metrics until it's painful.
zh: 所以我觉得，有时候创始人在分享指标这件事上过于乐观，直到吃了苦头。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so I do give everybody who wants to sort of play that game a cautionary
zh: 所以对于每个想要玩这种游戏的人，我都会给出一个警示

speaker: Unknown
en: But you see it playing out in the legal domain.
zh: 但你能在法律领域看到这一切在上演。

speaker: Unknown
en: I mean, you can't open X these days without Harvey posting some metrics and the Lagorres investors are all publishing their metrics.
zh: 我是说，现在你打开 X 都离不开 Harvey 发布一些指标，而 Lagorres 的投资人都在发布他们的指标。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's like non-stop.
zh: 简直没完没了。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's actually kind of funny.
zh: 其实挺有意思的。

speaker: Unknown
en: Who would have thought that the most popular thing on X most days of the week would be a debate about legal AI?
zh: 谁能想到一周里大多数日子 X 上最火的话题会是关于法律 AI 的辩论？

speaker: Unknown
en: It's so true.

speaker: Unknown
en: Also, Ramp is pretty savvy about sharing transactional data, sort of to say, oh, Anthropic is being adopted more aggressively right now by enterprises, or no, no, it's OpenAI.
zh: 另外，Ramp 在分享交易数据方面也挺精明的，大概是说，哦，Anthropic 现在被企业更积极地采用了，或者不不，是 OpenAI。

speaker: Unknown
en: Anyway, I give them a lot of credit.
zh: 总之，我很赞赏他们。

speaker: Unknown
en: I do wonder if you are worried in any way about rippling.
zh: 我确实想知道，你是否在任何程度上担心 Rippling。

speaker: Unknown
en: It really does seem like, whether or not he says it explicitly, they've got Ramp in their crosshairs.
zh: 看起来真的，不管他有没有明说，他们已经把 Ramp 瞄准在枪口上了。

speaker: Unknown
en: And Parker Conrad, no.
zh: 还有 Parker Conrad，不。

speaker: Unknown
en: I love Parker, you know, I've been friends with Parker forever.
zh: 我爱 Parker，你知道，我和 Parker 是很多年的朋友了。

speaker: Unknown
en: Rapp is not worried about Rippling.
zh: Rapp 不担心 Rippling。

speaker: Unknown
en: We're going to compete with Anthropic.
zh: 我们要和 Anthropic 竞争。

speaker: Unknown
en: That's the goal.
zh: 那就是目标。

speaker: Unknown
en: I want to be larger and more successful and more important than Anthropic.
zh: 我想变得比 Anthropic 更大、更成功、更重要。

speaker: Unknown
en: And you've seen some of the steps that we've taken recently.
zh: 而且你已经看到了我们最近采取的一些举措。

speaker: Unknown
en: The future
zh: 未来

speaker: Unknown
en: of the world is driven through tokens and equivalent, and RAMP's going to be the primary way people manage their token spend, how they optimize it, how they measure ROI, and that will lead us to collide probably with Anthropic in many ways.
zh: 是由 token 及等价物驱动的，而 RAMP 将成为人们管理 token 支出、优化支出、衡量 ROI 的主要方式，这大概会在很多方面让我们与 Anthropic 相撞。

speaker: Unknown
en: That is a bold statement.
zh: 这是一个大胆的宣言。

speaker: Unknown
en: I do wonder about some of the other tactics that we're seeing, which is companies that announce like valuations.
zh: 我确实想知道我们看到的其他一些策略，比如公司宣布估值。

speaker: Unknown
en: I mean, I've seen a couple of instances where it's been like within weeks and the valuation is multiple billions of dollars more than it was the last time.
zh: 我见过几个例子，就在几周之内，估值比上一次多了好几十亿美元。

speaker: Unknown
en: What do you think of that and how should people interpret what's happening out there?
zh: 你怎么看这件事，人们应该如何解读外面正在发生的情况？

speaker: Unknown
en: I mean, I would say we've done a few of those fast follow rounds.
zh: 我是说，我们也做过几次这种快速跟进轮。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's not our favorite thing to do.
zh: 那不是我们最喜欢做的事。

speaker: Unknown
en: We're probably pretty cautious and have a lot of debate about it.
zh: 我们可能相当谨慎，为此有过很多争论。

speaker: Unknown
en: But there is a belief that in the verticals that matter, a company that is successful will be worth a hell of a lot of money.
zh: 但有一种信念是，在那些重要的垂直领域里，一家成功的公司将会值非常非常多钱。

speaker: Unknown
en: Like, when I was starting a venture, which wasn't that long ago, 2013, a home run success, in the back of my mind anyway, was between a $10 billion and $50 billion outcome.
zh: 比如，当年我创业的时候，那也不是很久以前，2013 年，在我心目中，一个全垒打式的成功，是指 100 亿到 500 亿美元量级的结果。

speaker: Unknown
en: And the extreme end of, like, super success is $100 billion.
zh: 而极端的、超级成功的上限就是 1000 亿美元。

speaker: Unknown
en: Now I'd put at least one zero, you know, on that goal and possibly put a second zero.
zh: 现在我会在那个目标上至少再加一个零，你知道，可能会加两个零。

speaker: Unknown
en: So two orders of magnitude.
zh: 所以是两个数量级。

speaker: Unknown
en: So if you believe that that's true, so we talked about two companies that in venture timeframes, like within a fund cycle, plus or minus, have created a trillion dollars plus of value, it's now possible to dream that way.
zh: 所以如果你相信这是真的，我们刚才聊到了两家公司，在风投的时间尺度上，大约一个基金周期之内，就创造了一万亿美元以上的价值，现在可以这样做梦了。

speaker: Unknown
en: If that prediction is right that there might be more trillion-dollar outcomes created within a venture life of a fund or so, picking the right company and figuring out how to get capital in it at almost any price is not as crazy as it seems.
zh: 如果那个预测是对的，即在一个基金的存续期内左右可能创造出更多万亿美元量级的结果，那么选中正确的公司并想方设法以几乎任何价格把资本投进去，就没有看起来那么疯狂。

speaker: Unknown
en: I'll quote my former colleague at the Founders Fund, Brian Stingerman.
zh: 我来引用我在 Founders Fund 的前同事 Brian Stingerman 的话。

speaker: Unknown
en: He did a podcast recently with Jack Altman at Benchmark.
zh: 他最近和 Benchmark 的 Jack Altman 一起做了一期播客。

speaker: Unknown
en: And what Brian said is like, look, at Founders Fund, we were the 30th investor in Airbnb, but we made the second most money, $3 billion of returns.
zh: Brian 说的是，你看，在 Founders Fund，我们是 Airbnb 的第 30 个投资人，但我们赚了第二多的钱，30 亿美元的回报。

speaker: Unknown
en: Does it matter really that we spent $150 million to generate the $3 billion of returns and some people could have done it for 50 or 15?
zh: 我们花了 1.5 亿美元才产生这 30 亿美元的回报，而有些人本可以用 5000 万或 1500 万做到，这真的重要吗？

speaker: Unknown
en: Not really.
zh: 不重要。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's the $3 billion that really matters.
zh: 真正重要的是那 30 亿美元。

speaker: Unknown
en: So that's what most people are thinking.
zh: 大多数人就是这么想的。

speaker: Unknown
en: That said, I think identifying the winning companies is much more challenging than people realize, including my colleagues.
zh: 话虽如此，我认为识别出赢家公司比人们意识到的要困难得多，包括我的同事在内。

speaker: Unknown
en: For example, in the Ramp case, many people thought Brex was going to be a successful company.
zh: 比如，在 Ramp 这个例子里，很多人曾以为 Brex 会是一家成功的公司。

speaker: Unknown
en: If you had chased Brex at every valuation, the last couple rounds did not make money.
zh: 如果你在每一轮估值都追投 Brex，最后几轮是没有赚到钱的。

speaker: Unknown
en: You know, maybe they got their capital back or something like that, but they're risk-adjusted and time-adjusted, not particularly attractive.
zh: 你知道，也许他们拿回了本金什么的，但按风险调整和时间调整来算，并不特别有吸引力。

speaker: Unknown
en: Who knows how OpenAI versus Anthropic is going to play out long-term.
zh: 谁知道 OpenAI 对 Anthropic 长期会怎么发展。

speaker: Unknown
en: But a year and a half ago, everybody was like, OpenAI is a monopoly.
zh: 但一年半以前，每个人都说，OpenAI 是垄断者。

speaker: Unknown
en: Then everybody's like, now, oh, no, it's Anthropic.
zh: 然后每个人又说，现在，哦不，是 Anthropic。

speaker: Unknown
en: And now people are shifting back a little bit more OpenAI.
zh: 而现在人们又稍微转向回 OpenAI 一点。

speaker: Unknown
en: Which of those companies are you powering money into?
zh: 你正在往哪些公司里砸钱?

speaker: Unknown
en: I don't know how to choose.
zh: 我不知道该怎么选。

speaker: Unknown
en: Or LegalAI?
zh: 还是 LegalAI?

speaker: Unknown
en: Would you give, Winston just announced, you know, they're financing a $550 million, 15.5 bill, like, Tuesday.
zh: 你会给……Winston 刚刚宣布了,你知道,他们在融资 5.5 亿,155 亿,像是,周二。

speaker: Unknown
en: Would you power a billion dollars into Harvey, or Lagora, or none of the above, or some startup in legal AI that none of us have heard of yet?
zh: 你会往 Harvey 砸 10 亿美元,还是 Lagora,还是以上都不选,还是某个我们谁都还没听说过的法律 AI 创业公司?

speaker: Unknown
en: I don't think that's such an obvious call.
zh: 我不认为这是一个那么显而易见的选择。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so I'm sitting around, and would I write a $300 million check to any of them?
zh: 所以我坐在这里想,我会给他们中任何一家开一张 3 亿美元的支票吗?

speaker: Unknown
en: I don't know how to do that right now.
zh: 我现在不知道该怎么做到这一点。

speaker: Unknown
en: Do I take Dekacon versus Sierra versus whoever?
zh: 我该选 Dekacon 还是 Sierra 还是随便谁?

speaker: Unknown
en: Almost in every AI vertical, the art of choosing where to do that
zh: 几乎在每一个 AI 垂直领域,选择把钱投到哪里的艺术

speaker: Unknown
en: is much more difficult, I think, than people realize.
zh: 我认为比人们意识到的要难得多。

speaker: Unknown
en: I'm sure that's true.
zh: 我确信这是真的。

speaker: Unknown
en: And unfortunately right ahead, but I did want to ask you, because I think there's founders in the audience, I did see you appear with Vinod on Jack Altman's podcast, which I really enjoy.
zh: 不幸的是马上就要结束了,但我确实想问你,因为我认为观众里有创始人,我确实看到你和 Vinod 一起上了 Jack Altman 的播客,我真的很喜欢那个播客。

speaker: Unknown
en: You talked about A-plus players and basically your ability to discern them in like a few minutes.
zh: 你谈到了 A 级人才,以及你基本上能在几分钟内辨别出他们的能力。

speaker: Unknown
en: And of course in Silicon Valley and here too, so many smart, polished speakers who can tell a story and articulate a vision.
zh: 当然在硅谷,在这里也一样,有那么多聪明、打磨得很好的演讲者,他们会讲故事,能清晰地阐述愿景。

speaker: Unknown
en: Like there's so many superhumans in this industry.
zh: 就像这个行业里有那么多超人。

speaker: Unknown
en: What makes somebody more superhuman?
zh: 是什么让一个人更加超人?

speaker: Unknown
en: And where have you made a mistake on that front?
zh: 而你在这方面犯过什么错误?

speaker: Unknown
en: So there's one formulation, there's a second formulation, maybe a third formulation.
zh: 所以有一种表述,还有第二种表述,也许还有第三种表述。

speaker: Unknown
en: First formulation is I am personally looking for someone who is in the top one to ten basis points on any particular trait.
zh: 第一种表述是,我个人在寻找在某一个特定特质上处于最顶尖万分之一到千分之十的人。

speaker: Unknown
en: It doesn't matter, like polished, they can be completely introverted and completely unpolished.
zh: 无所谓,比如是否打磨得体,他们可以完全内向、完全不修边幅。

speaker: Unknown
en: But they're like the smartest person.
zh: 但他们就是最聪明的人。

speaker: Unknown
en: We're going to be extremely polished and it's the greatest salesperson you've ever met in your life.
zh: 我们要找的也可能是极其打磨得体、是你一生中见过的最伟大的销售员的人。

speaker: Unknown
en: And you just know instantly.
zh: 而你立刻就能知道。

speaker: Unknown
en: Or it's a combination of two traits that are very rarely found together.
zh: 或者是两种极少同时出现的特质的组合。

speaker: Unknown
en: This is my Max Levchin example.
zh: 这就是我的 Max Levchin 例子。

speaker: Unknown
en: Max is a first-rate technologist and he's got a very top-tier business acumen.
zh: Max 是一流的技术专家,同时他有着非常顶级商业嗅觉。

speaker: Unknown
en: Those do not normally match.
zh: 这两者通常不会同时出现。

speaker: Unknown
en: In fact, this is in hindsight.
zh: 事实上,这是事后回想。

speaker: Unknown
en: Reid Hoffman told me this about Max in December 2000.
zh: Reid Hoffman 在 2000 年 12 月告诉过我关于 Max 的事。

speaker: Unknown
en: I was preparing for my first one-on-one meeting with Max, and Reid Hoffman sits me down and says, this is what you need to know about Max.
zh: 我当时在准备和 Max 的第一次一对一会议,Reid Hoffman 让我坐下,说,这是你需要了解的关于 Max 的事。

speaker: Unknown
en: He's as sharp as they come in a business acumen sense, so don't try to compete with him that way.
zh: 他在商业嗅觉方面锋利得不得了,所以不要试图在那种方式上和他竞争。

speaker: Unknown
en: And he's a first-rate technologist, and there's five people in Silicon Valley that have that Venn diagram overlap.
zh: 而且他是一流的技术专家,在硅谷只有五个人拥有那种维恩图交集。

speaker: Unknown
en: Proved to be a pretty good call by Reed, honestly, in the next 26 years.
zh: 说实话,在接下来的 26 年里,这被证明是 Reed 的一个相当准确的判断。

speaker: Unknown
en: So Jack Dorsey was kind of that way.
zh: 所以 Jack Dorsey 也有点那种样子。

speaker: Unknown
en: Jack's pretty first-rate business strategist, actually pretty top-tier designer too, or at least design taste, and pretty good technologist.
zh: Jack 其实是相当一流的商业战略家,实际上也是相当顶尖的设计师,或者至少是设计品味,还是相当不错的技术专家。

speaker: Unknown
en: So he has three.
zh: 所以他有三个。

speaker: Unknown
en: So I think the rare overlap Venn diagram, I was actually talking on this podcast recently about my husband who just showed up, about he has an unusually Venn diagram overlap of he can speak to tech people and speak to
zh: 所以我认为这种罕见的维恩图交集,我最近其实在这个播客上谈到过我丈夫,他刚刚来了,谈到他有一种不寻常的维恩图交集:他既能和科技界的人交谈,又能和

speaker: Unknown
en: political people and almost no one can speak both of their languages and that became his superpower initially.
zh: 政治界的人交谈,而几乎没有人能同时说这两种语言,这最初成了他的超能力。

speaker: Unknown
en: And then third is there's these rare people that can walk you through what Chris Dixon and Balaji used to call the intellectual maze and they blogged about it, where they can just tell you where they are today and how they're going to build a company in a vertical and industry and walk you through every single move and account for all the trapdoors and mistakes that everybody's ever made through history.
zh: 然后第三种是,有这些罕见的人,他们能带你走完 Chris Dixon 和 Balaji 曾经所说的智力迷宫,他们还为此写过博客,就是他们能直接告诉你他们今天在哪里,以及他们要如何在某个垂直领域和行业里建立一家公司,带你走完每一步,并且把历史上所有人都踩过的所有陷阱和错误都考虑在内。

speaker: Unknown
en: They tell you this story, and actually, it's even more impressive if you have contacts, like someone like me in financial services or something, and you're just, wow.
zh: 他们给你讲这个故事,实际上,如果你有人脉,比如像我这样在金融服务领域或其他什么领域的人,那就更令人印象深刻了,你就是会觉得,哇。

speaker: Unknown
en: Like, this person has a map of the planet.
zh: 就像,这个人对这个星球有一张地图。

speaker: Unknown
en: That is instantly fundable, too.
zh: 那也是立刻就能获得融资的。

speaker: Unknown
en: That's actually the rarest of the three, by the way.
zh: 顺便说一句,那其实是三者中最罕见的。

speaker: Unknown
en: But there was a company recently, let's say in the last year in New York, that does AI infrastructure, which is something I thought I would never touch in my life.
zh: 但最近有一家公司,可以说是去年在纽约,做 AI 基础设施,那是我曾以为这辈子都不会碰的东西。

speaker: Unknown
en: Met this founder.
zh: 见了这位创始人。

speaker: Unknown
en: It is urgent that I sort of meet the founder, because I was the only partner in New York.
zh: 我见这位创始人是很紧迫的事,因为我是纽约唯一的合伙人。

speaker: Unknown
en: And he just walked me through this map and I was like, oh my God.
zh: 然后他就带我走完这张地图,我当时就想,我的天。

speaker: Unknown
en: Like I've never heard anybody in an impressive way walk me through how AI infrastructure works and should work in account for all the moving pieces of what other people are doing or not doing.
zh: 就像,我从没听过有人以一种令人印象深刻的方式给我讲解 AI 基础设施是如何运作的、应该如何运作,并把其他人在做或没做的所有变量都考虑进去。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I texted my colleague who sent it to me and I was like, no brainer, please invest now, close.
zh: 我给我那位把信息发给我的同事发了消息，我说，这还用想吗，现在就投资，赶紧敲定。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's an area I know nothing about, but the map was so impressive.
zh: 这是我完全不了解的领域，但那张图（map）实在太令人震撼了。

speaker: Unknown
en: It just blew me away.
zh: 它就是把我给震撼到了。

speaker: Unknown
en: There's a third thing, so I recently got asked by my colleagues, this question comes up a lot, but I got asked on an offsite to sort of teach my colleagues how to assess founders.
zh: 还有第三件事，我最近被同事们问到了这个问题，这个问题经常出现，我在一次外出团建时被要求教同事们如何评估创始人。

speaker: Unknown
en: I was like, oh my god, this is, they've heard me say all this stuff, I'm like, it's not working because you guys are not copying this.
zh: 我当时说，天哪，这……他们都已经听我说过所有这些内容了，我心想，这没用啊，因为你们都没有照着学。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I was frustrated, but they're like, no, Adam, you've got to speak about it.
zh: 我很沮丧，但他们说，不，Adam，你必须把它讲出来。

speaker: Unknown
en: So I went back to as my last chief of staff.
zh: 于是我回去找了我上一任幕僚长（chief of staff）。

speaker: Unknown
en: And he's phenomenal and very talented, shadowed me for like 18 months, like 24-7 sort of thing.
zh: 他非常出色也很有才华，跟着我观摩了大概 18 个月，几乎是 24 小时不间断那种。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I wrote to him like, from your observation and vantage point, what am I actually looking for?
zh: 我给他写消息说，从你的观察和视角来看，我到底在看什么？

speaker: Unknown
en: And he wrote me five bullet point text.
zh: 他给我回了五条要点式的文字。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I wound up using three of the five instead of my normal speech.
zh: 结果我用了那五条里的三条，代替了我平时那段讲稿。

speaker: Unknown
en: And he had picked up on certain things.
zh: 他捕捉到了某些东西。

speaker: Unknown
en: The one that most applies to your question was, he said, the first thing you're going to do is people who are trying to raise money, basically store in cash mode, in a technology sense, the answers to every investor question.
zh: 其中最适用于你这个问题的那条，他说，你要做的第一件事是，那些来融资的人，基本上以缓存（cash）模式存储了每一个投资人问题的答案，从技术角度说。

speaker: Unknown
en: And he's like, the first thing you do at every meeting is you're going to invalidate their cash right away, you're going to find a way to throw it out, and you're going to notice a time to first new token
zh: 他说，你在每次会上做的第一件事，就是立刻让他们的缓存失效，你要想办法把它清掉，然后你会注意到「到第一个新 token 的时间」（time to first new token）

speaker: Unknown
en: And then the quality of that, and that's going to be like half your assessment.
zh: 以及那个输出的质量，而这大概会占你评估的一半。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I was like, wow, I'd actually never thought I was doing that.
zh: 我当时说，哇，我从没意识到我是在这么做。

speaker: Unknown
en: But as soon as you wrote it to me, I was like, oh, my God, that's exactly what I'm doing.
zh: 但他一写给我，我立刻就说，哦天哪，我做的正是这个。

speaker: Unknown
en: And then I could teach that as a skill.
zh: 然后我就可以把它作为一项技能来教了。

speaker: Unknown
en: Now, the problem is invalidating a founder who's pretty good's cash requires a lot of generally experience.
zh: 现在，问题在于，让一个水平不错的创始人的缓存失效，需要大量的通用经验。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's not too easy for a junior VC to do that.
zh: 对一个资历浅的 VC 来说这并不容易做到。

speaker: Unknown
en: And also, you have to do it in a deft enough style that people will tolerate it.
zh: 而且，你还得用足够巧妙的风格去做，让人能够接受。

speaker: Unknown
en: You can't just tell a founder, like, oh, that's stupid.
zh: 你不能直接跟创始人说，哦，这太蠢了。

speaker: Unknown
en: Like, you just start from scratch.
zh: 之类的话，比如你就从头再来吧。

speaker: Unknown
en: Could you just like ask some orthogonal question at work?
zh: 能不能就在工作中问一个正交的问题之类的？

speaker: Unknown
en: Yeah, it's like basically find something that you know a fair amount about ideally and basically probe pretty aggressively in I don't believe that's true or it's not consistent with this data point or it's not consistent with this company or it's not consistent with this experience and force them to re-derive it and see what they do.
zh: 是的，基本上就是找一个你 Ideally 比较了解的领域，然后相当激进地去探究，比如「我不相信这是真的」或者「这与这个数据点不一致」或者「这与这家公司不一致」或者「这与这个经验不一致」，逼他们重新推导，看他们的反应。

speaker: Unknown
en: And can they absorb
zh: 以及他们能否吸收

speaker: Unknown
en: And build on it.
zh: 并在此基础上构建。

speaker: Unknown
en: The ones that are most impressive actually will remix some of your critiques and then have a new answer.
zh: 最令人印象深刻的那类人，实际上会把你的部分批评重新混搭（remix），然后给出一个新答案。

speaker: Unknown
en: And that's just like incredibly impressive.
zh: 那种表现真是令人难以置信地出色。

speaker: Unknown
en: That's like almost an instant invest decision.
zh: 那几乎就是一个立刻决定投资的信号。

speaker: Unknown
en: If they can take your ideas or critiques, absorb them on the fly and come up with a refined answer that's still mostly theirs.
zh: 如果他们能把你的想法或批评，即时吸收进去，并给出一个主要仍属于他们自己的更完善的答案。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's like remixing a song on the fly, but taking a David Guedes song and remixing it successfully is very challenging.
zh: 这就像即兴混搭一首歌，但把一首 David Guedes 的歌成功混搭是非常难的。

speaker: Unknown
en: Well, founders, now you know the secret.
zh: 好了，创始人们，现在你们知道秘诀了。

speaker: Unknown
en: Yeah, pretty much.
zh: 是啊，差不多就是这样。

speaker: Unknown
en: Keith, thank you so much for coming.
zh: Keith，非常感谢你来。

speaker: Unknown
en: Pleasure.
zh: 我的荣幸。

speaker: Unknown
en: Thanks for the invite.
zh: 谢谢你们的邀请。

speaker: Unknown
en: Hi, Jacob, if you're back there somewhere.
zh: 嗨，Jacob，如果你还在后面某处的话。

speaker: Unknown
en: The Strictly VC Download podcast is hosted by TechCrunch Editor-in-Chief Connie Loizos and me, Alex Gove of Strictly VC.
zh: 《Strictly VC Download》播客由 TechCrunch 主编 Connie Loizos 和我——Strictly VC 的 Alex Gove 共同主持。

speaker: Unknown
en: Strictly VC Download is produced by Maggie Nye with editing assistance by Teresa Lancansolo and Kel.
zh: 《Strictly VC Download》由 Maggie Nye 制作，Teresa Lancansolo 和 Kel 提供剪辑协助。

speaker: Unknown
en: Thanks for listening.
zh: 感谢收听。

speaker: Unknown
en: We'll see you back here next week.
zh: 我们下周再见。
